pain_points.title: Seal Failure & IGU Fogging
pain_points.description: The seal between double- or triple-pane glass fails, allowing moisture between panes.
pain_points.why_buyers_care: Most common window failure. Fix costs $200-400 per window even under warranty because most warranties cover parts but not labor.
pain_points.surfacing_rule: If product warranty excludes IGU seal after any period, or is parts-only for seal replacement, surface as Buyer Consideration

pain_points.title: Warranty Registration Deadlines
pain_points.description: Many warranties require registration within 30-60 days of purchase or installation. Missing the deadline can reduce coverage by 50-75%.
pain_points.why_buyers_care: Buyers often don't know about the registration requirement until they need to file a claim years later.
pain_points.financial_impact: Full warranty value at risk — can reduce 20-year coverage to 5 years
pain_points.surfacing_rule: If product warranty requires registration within any time period to maintain full coverage, surface as Buyer Consideration

pain_points.title: Parts-Only Warranty Coverage
pain_points.description: Many window warranties cover replacement parts but not the labor to install them. Labor often costs more than the part itself.
pain_points.why_buyers_care: A 'lifetime warranty' sounds comprehensive but covers $50 in parts while you pay $300 in labor.
pain_points.financial_impact: $150-400 per window for labor on component replacement
pain_points.surfacing_rule: If warranty is parts-only for any component, or labor is excluded after any period, surface as Buyer Consideration

pain_points.title: Non-Transferable or Limited Transfer Warranty
pain_points.description: Warranty either doesn't transfer to the next owner or transfers with significantly reduced coverage.
pain_points.why_buyers_care: Reduces resale value. A buyer paying premium prices expects the warranty to follow the product, not the original purchaser.
pain_points.financial_impact: Indirect — reduces home resale value by the remaining warranty value
pain_points.surfacing_rule: If warranty is non-transferable or has significant reduction on transfer, surface as Buyer Consideration

pain_points.title: Limited Dealer or Service Network
pain_points.description: Product is only available through limited channels or direct-to-consumer, making service, replacement parts, and warranty claims difficult.
pain_points.why_buyers_care: When something breaks in 5 years, you need a local dealer who can order parts and arrange service. No local presence means shipping windows across the country.
pain_points.surfacing_rule: If product lacks a broad dealer/service network or is only available direct-to-consumer, surface as Buyer Consideration

pain_points.title: Lead Time and Availability Issues
pain_points.description: Product has long lead times (8+ weeks) or frequent availability problems that can delay construction schedules.
pain_points.why_buyers_care: A 12-week lead time on windows can delay an entire construction project. Contractors may need to hold crews or pay penalties.
pain_points.surfacing_rule: If documented lead times exceed 8 weeks or availability issues are a pattern, surface as Buyer Consideration

pain_points.title: Warranty Claim Difficulties
pain_points.description: Brand has documented patterns of denying warranty claims, slow service response, or requiring extensive documentation.
pain_points.why_buyers_care: A warranty is only as good as the company standing behind it. Patterns of claim denial turn a 20-year warranty into paper decoration.
pain_points.financial_impact: Full replacement cost if claims are denied — $300-1500+ per window
pain_points.surfacing_rule: If professional sources or curated evidence report consistent patterns of warranty claim difficulties, surface as Buyer Consideration

pain_points.title: Finish Degradation in UV-Heavy Climates
pain_points.description: Exterior finish (paint, coating, vinyl color) degrades prematurely in high UV environments, causing chalking, fading, or peeling.
pain_points.why_buyers_care: A $600 window that looks washed out in 3 years costs another $200+ per window to refinish. Southern and western exposures are worst.
pain_points.financial_impact: $150-300 per window for refinishing or $400-800 for replacement
pain_points.surfacing_rule: If evidence shows finish degradation patterns, especially in UV-heavy climates, surface as Buyer Consideration

pain_points.title: Proprietary Hardware and Replacement Parts
pain_points.description: Product uses proprietary hardware (locks, balances, operators) that can only be sourced from the manufacturer.
pain_points.why_buyers_care: If the manufacturer discontinues the product line or goes out of business, replacement parts become impossible to find.
pain_points.financial_impact: $100-400 per window for custom part sourcing or workarounds
pain_points.surfacing_rule: If product uses proprietary hardware that cannot be sourced from third parties, surface as Buyer Consideration

pain_points.title: Class Action or Pattern Defect History
pain_points.description: Brand has class action lawsuits or documented pattern defects in the past decade related to product failure.
pain_points.why_buyers_care: Past pattern defects suggest systemic quality control issues that may not be fully resolved, even if the specific issue was 'fixed'.
pain_points.financial_impact: Varies — potential total window replacement if defect recurs
pain_points.surfacing_rule: If brand has class action or pattern defect lawsuits within the past 10 years, surface as Buyer Consideration with plain language description
